sourceDiscrepancies.sourceNote: The native solution substitution prints 10000 °K while the question uses 10 000 K; the degree sign is retained.

The source says 12 stars form a dodecahedron; the unlabelled drawing has the native dodecahedral geometry. The key’s “5th farthest” differs from the question’s five closest stars. The last displayed cosine expression omits degree signs on its sine arguments; all printed forms are retained.

The final formula uses v_p for 1004 m/s after part(c) gave v_p=1076.3 m/s in a different frame. The distinct printed numeric constants are retained; G, Earth mass and Earth radius differ slightly from the separately attributed undated common reference.

The matter explanation says “total energy density ... remains unchanged” while deriving density proportional to a^-3. Its radiation proportionality prints a_m(t), although the following derivation uses a_r(t). Both native expressions are retained. The key-only Friedmann variable clarification is attributed separately.

The key calls the a^3 proportional to T^2 relation “Kepler’s second law”; this printed name is retained. Its spelling “Stephen Boltzmann” and “Stephen Boltzman’s” also remains literal. The solar apparent magnitude -26.74 is a key-only question supplement, not silently added to the original statement.

The orbital radius expression is printed as sqrt(GM/omega^3); no cubic root or different omega exponent is substituted. The first SNR evaluation has N^2 rather than the question’s N_r^2. The part(d) intermediate angular velocity conflicts with its given plate scale, elapsed time and final 1.31 arcsec/min. These printed expressions, results and all marking acceptance notes are retained. The solution’s own sunlight/graybody wording remains as printed.

The aphelion paragraph prints M=π/2 and ν=M=π in the same sentence. Two intermediate part(c) terms print sin M and sin²(M) where adjacent lines use L; native notation and the final boxed expression are retained. The final diagram has horizontal δ and vertical Δα, while the preceding prose says a plot of δ against Δα; the source plot is retained with its original axis labels.
